blocks.raw: ### Hydra iOS SDK release [1.6.0](https://github.com/Capillary/hydra-sdk-ios-packages/releases/tag/1.6.0)
blocks.text: Hydra iOS SDK release 1.6.0

blocks.raw:
* Performance Improvements
  * Used backgroundContext for CRUD operations to improve Core Data efficiency.
  * Optimized database operations using asynchronous perform methods.
  * Created a separate queue for thread-safe resource access.
* Bug Fixes
  * Resolved issues in event handling and pull notifications.
* Feature Enhancements
  * Added public methods to update various Hydra attributes.
  * Added completion blocks for critical asynchronous operations like DLR event reporting and database insertions.
* Database and Notification Handling
  * Set mergePolicy for the backgroundContext to handle conflicts gracefully.
  * Improved unread notification count retrieval with a dedicated method.
  * Updated notifications as read when a user interacts with them.
  * Enhanced pull approach by saving valid notifications into the database before further processing.

blocks.raw: ## Editing messages in a live journey
blocks.text: Editing messages in a live journey

blocks.raw:
Previously, when editing a journey, a new version was created, but customers who had already entered a specific journey version could continue in the same version and, therefore, receive the older content.\
With this feature, we now offer support for moving users from one version of the journey to the next while going live with the newer version, enabling real-time updates without stopping/sunsetting the journey.
This allows for greater flexibility and optimization based on ongoing performance.

blocks.raw: ## Enhancing Reporting - Support for all types of Audience Groups as filters
blocks.text: Enhancing Reporting - Support for all types of Audience Groups as filters

blocks.raw:
Previously, only filter-based audience groups were supported as filters in the reports. As a part of this minor enhancement, we have enriched reporting to support all types of audience groups—combined, uploaded, or filter-based as filters.\
This will enable brands to compare reports across a combination of audience groups, including uploaded ones.
You can find more information [here](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/add-audience-group).

blocks.raw: ## Enhanced Reporting on Concept Hierarchy
blocks.text: Enhanced Reporting on Concept Hierarchy

blocks.raw: Building on our commitment to empowering brand and business teams with more relevant reporting structures, we’ve now extended the flexibility of our Concept Hierarchy feature in Insights to support deeper and more complex store structures.
blocks.text: Building on our commitment to empowering brand and business teams with more relevant reporting structures, we’ve now extended the flexibility of our Concept Hierarchy feature in Insights to support deeper and more complex store structures.

blocks.raw: Previously, Concept Hierarchy allowed the grouping of stores across up to 3 levels, limiting how deeply brands could model their operational hierarchies. To address the growing need for more granular and business-specific reporting, we’ve enhanced the hierarchy support to allow up to 7 levels, enabling significantly more detailed drill-downs and performance comparisons.

blocks.raw: ## Reducing the upload based segments availability time from T+2 -> T+1
blocks.text: Reducing the upload based segments availability time from T+2 -> T+1

blocks.raw: Previously, when brands needed to create complex segments using files created based on Databricks notebooks, the process took T+2 days - one day for ETL and another for syncing the uploaded file via FTP. This delayed time-sensitive campaigns & promotions.
blocks.text: Previously, when brands needed to create complex segments using files created based on Databricks notebooks, the process took T+2 days - one day for ETL and another for syncing the uploaded file via FTP. This delayed time-sensitive campaigns & promotions.

blocks.raw: We’ve now reduced this delay to T+1 day by introducing SQL traits based on complex business logic. These attributes are processed during ETL and made available directly to the segment builder the next day, removing the need for an additional sync step.

blocks.raw: ## Improved Timezone Handling in Rewards Catalog
blocks.text: Improved Timezone Handling in Rewards Catalog

blocks.raw: Previously, reward timings in the get APIs were returned in the server’s timezone, often leading to confusion for teams working across regions. For instance, if a reward was set for 25th April, 10:00 AM Dubai time, it might incorrectly appear as 11:30 AM IST, without any timezone label, just because the server was running in India timezone.
blocks.text: Previously, reward timings in the get APIs were returned in the server’s timezone, often leading to confusion for teams working across regions. blocks.raw: ## Configurable Rounding Methods For Reward Currencies In Advanced Program Settings

blocks.raw: You can already set the number of decimal points to round reward values. Now, you can also select a rounding method for Reward Currencies (points and alternate currencies) based on the decimal points configured.

blocks.raw:
**Example:**\
25.8751 points are to be allocated to a customer and the round-off is set to two decimal places. If the rounding method selected is “Ceiling”, the points are rounded to two decimal places and rounded up to 25.88.

blocks.raw:

* The following rounding methods are available: Ceiling, Floor, Round Half Up, Round Half Down, Round Half Even.
* This enhancement gives brands more control over how reward currency balances are handled, ensuring consistency in point calculations.

blocks.text: A new API has been introduced to retrieve a consolidated summary of all benefits (points, badges, rewards, and alternate currencies) a customer earned from a specific loyalty promotion.

blocks.text: Sending loyalty-related communications via WhatsApp and other channels using the Central Communications Engine is now integrated with Loyalty+ workflows.

blocks.raw: ## New Issual Restriction for Loyalty Promotions\*\*
blocks.text: New Issual Restriction for Loyalty Promotions**

blocks.raw: Loyalty promotions already let you set limits on the number of times a promotion can be issued to a single customer and redeemed by a customer. Now, you can also restrict the total number of times a promotion is issued across your entire customer base with a new overall limit.
blocks.text: Loyalty promotions already let you set limits on the number of times a promotion can be issued to a single customer and redeemed by a customer. Now, you can also restrict the total number of times a promotion is issued across your entire customer base with a new overall limit.

blocks.raw: **What’s New:**
blocks.text: What’s New:

blocks.raw:
* Set a limit on the total number of times a loyalty promotion can be issued to all customers within a brand.
* Note: Leave the field blank to allow unlimited issuals (no capping).
blocks.text: Set a limit on the total number of times a loyalty promotion can be issued to all customers within a brand.Note: Leave the field blank to allow unlimited issuals (no capping).

blocks.raw:
**Example:**\
A brand creates a promotion with a maximum issual limit of 1000. This means the promotion can be issued to customers a total of 1000 times across the entire brand. Once this threshold is reached, the promotion will not be issued to more customers even if they are eligible.

blocks.raw: ## New Expression to Track Promised Points in Workflows
blocks.text: New Expression to Track Promised Points in Workflows

blocks.raw: You can already track points issued to customers after a transaction in workflows. Now, workflows support tracking promised points (non-redeemable points with delayed accrual) for greater flexibility in loyalty campaigns.
blocks.text: You can already track points issued to customers after a transaction in workflows. Now, workflows support tracking promised points (non-redeemable points with delayed accrual) for greater flexibility in loyalty campaigns.

blocks.raw: **What’s New:**
blocks.text: What’s New:

blocks.raw:
* A new attribute **promisedPoints** to track total promised points issued for a transaction.
* The attribute has two sub-attributes:
* **promisedPointsForUser:** Tracks promised points issued to an individual user in a transaction.
* **promisedPointsForUserGroup:** Tracks promised points issued to a user group in a transaction.
blocks.text: A new attribute promisedPoints to track total promised points issued for a transaction.The attribute has two sub-attributes:promisedPointsForUser: Tracks promised points issued to an individual user in a transaction.promisedPointsForUserGroup: Tracks promised points issued to a user group in a transaction.

target.note: normalise `*`/`+` markers to `-`

blocks.raw:
**Example:**\
Trigger a message when the promised points issued for a transaction is more than 300 points. To track this, use the expression in the loyalty workflows: **currentTxn.promisedPoints>= 300** and create the message action to send a message to the customer.
blocks.text: Example:Trigger a message when the promised points issued for a transaction is more than 300 points. To track this, use the expression in the loyalty workflows: currentTxn.promisedPoints>= 300 and create the message action to send a message to the customer.

blocks.raw: ## New Workflow Action: Convert Promised Alternate Currencies to Redeemable Alternate Currencies
blocks.text: New Workflow Action: Convert Promised Alternate Currencies to Redeemable Alternate Currencies

blocks.raw: A new workflow action has been introduced to convert promised alternate currencies (e.g., "Gold Coins") to redeemable based on rules specified for transactional updates.
blocks.text: A new workflow action has been introduced to convert promised alternate currencies (e.g., "Gold Coins") to redeemable based on rules specified for transactional updates.

blocks.raw: **What’s New:**
blocks.text: What’s New:

blocks.raw:
* Convert promised alternate currencies to redeemable currencies immediately or after an item’s return period has expired and the customer has not made any returns.
* Notes:
  * This action is supported only for the TransactionUpdate customer activity.
  * Promised alternate currencies do not affect tier upgrades/downgrades until converted to redeemable.
blocks.text: Convert promised alternate currencies to redeemable currencies immediately or after an item’s return period has expired and the customer has not made any returns.Notes:This action is supported only for the TransactionUpdate customer activity.Promised alternate currencies do not affect tier upgrades/downgrades until converted to redeemable.

blocks.raw:
**Example:**\
Reward customers with 50 promised "Travel Miles" after a flight booking. These miles convert to redeemable miles 30 days later if no cancellations occur. If the customer is qualified for a tier upgrade, they are upgraded to a higher tier once the “Travel Miles” are redeemable.
blocks.text: Example:Reward customers with 50 promised "Travel Miles" after a flight booking. These miles convert to redeemable miles 30 days later if no cancellations occur. If the customer is qualified for a tier upgrade, they are upgraded to a higher tier once the “Travel Miles” are redeemable.

blocks.raw: ## Month-Based Moving Window Tracking for Workflows
blocks.text: Month-Based Moving Window Tracking for Workflows

blocks.raw: Moving window tracking, which already supports days to track customer activities over a rolling period, now includes months for more flexible reward calculations.
blocks.text: Moving window tracking, which already supports days to track customer activities over a rolling period, now includes months for more flexible reward calculations.

blocks.raw: **What’s New:**
blocks.text: What’s New:

blocks.raw:
* Month-based tracking: Define moving windows using full calendar months (e.g., track activity over 1 or 3 months).
* Windows align with month boundaries from the first day of the month to the last day of the month.
* Track current month: Set the window to 0 months to start from the 1st day of the current month.
blocks.text: Month-based tracking: Define moving windows using full calendar months (e.g., track activity over 1 or 3 months).Windows align with month boundaries from the first day of the month to the last day of the month.Track current month: Set the window to 0 months to start from the 1st day of the current month.

target.note: normalise `*`/`+` markers to `-`

blocks.raw: **Example:** A tracker rewards 200 bonus points if a customer spends $1,000 in a 1-month window. Purchases on March 10 and April 10 are tracked from March 1–April 30. A purchase on May 1 shifts the window to April 1–May 31, dropping March data.
blocks.text: Example: A tracker rewards 200 bonus points if a customer spends $1,000 in a 1-month window. Purchases on March 10 and April 10 are tracked from March 1–April 30. A purchase on May 1 shifts the window to April 1–May 31, dropping March data.

blocks.raw: ## Points Unlock API Now Supports Alternate Currencies
blocks.text: Points Unlock API Now Supports Alternate Currencies

blocks.raw: The Points Unlock API already lets you convert promised points into redeemable points. Now, you can also use this API to convert promised alternate currencies into redeemable alternate currencies.
blocks.text: The Points Unlock API already lets you convert promised points into redeemable points. Now, you can also use this API to convert promised alternate currencies into redeemable alternate currencies.

blocks.raw: **What’s New:**
blocks.text: What’s New:

blocks.raw:
* Convert both promised points and alternate currencies (e.g., gold coins, stamps) to redeemable currencies in a single API call.
* Note: All promised reward currencies (points and alternate currencies) are unlocked simultaneously when using the API.

* Unified target prorating: Choose from four existing strategies for reward calculation:\
  Defined Target, Achieved Value, Achieved Value Above Defined Target and Qualifying value

blocks.raw: # Introducing Dev Console - New Capillary tool built to optimize operations for integration platforms
blocks.text: Introducing Dev Console - New Capillary tool built to optimize operations for integration platforms

blocks.raw: **Devconsole**, is a robust Capillary tool built to optimize operations for integration platforms. Devconsole consolidates all features previously available in the **APITester** portal, removing the need for separate access and onboarding.
blocks.text: Devconsole, is a robust Capillary tool built to optimize operations for integration platforms. Devconsole consolidates all features previously available in the APITester portal, removing the need for separate access and onboarding.

blocks.raw: Users can now log in seamlessly via the **Intouch portal**, reducing operational delays.
blocks.text: Users can now log in seamlessly via the Intouch portal, reducing operational delays.

blocks.raw: **Enhanced capabilities include:**
blocks.text: Enhanced capabilities include:

blocks.raw:
* Tenant-specific log access
* Metrics monitoring
* CI/CD support for Classic extensions
* MongoDB management
blocks.text: Tenant-specific log accessMetrics monitoringCI/CD support for Classic extensionsMongoDB management

blocks.text: Three new access groups are also intriduced in Devconsole to streamline user permissions and enhance functionality:

blocks.raw:
* **Dev Console External Developer**

  * View access to:

    * Package Manager
    * Platform Metrics
    * Log Viewer
    * DB Audit Logs
    * Extension Configurations
  * Permissions:

    * Execute **read** queries
    * Raise requests for **write** queries and **new config** setups

* **Dev Console External Tech Lead**

  * Includes all Developer permissions
  * Additional capabilities:

    * Build Classic extensions via Package Manager
    * Approve write queries
    * Approve config requests

* **Dev Console Brand POC**

  * Restricted to viewing **Platform Metrics** only
